olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $P$ be a point inside triangle $ABC$. Points $D,E,$ and $F$ are constructed on segments $BC,CA,$ and $AB$, respectively, so that
$$BD=DC,\qquad CE=EA,\qquad AF=FB.$$
Lines $AP,BP,$ and $CP$ intersect lines $EF,FD,$ and $DE$ at points $X,Y,$ and $Z$, respectively. Prove that
$$
\frac{XP}{AP}+ rac{YP}{BP}+ rac{ZP}{CP}=1.
$$
figure_description: Triangle with medians and cevian intersections through an interior point.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Consider a $2n\times2n$ chessboard whose rows and columns are each labeled from $1$ to $2n$. Two rooks are placed on the chessboard so that the squares occupied by the rooks lie in different rows and different columns. We say that the rooks are in harmonious positions if the pair of row labels and the pair of column labels have the same parity.

Find the number of subsets of squares of a $2n\times2n$ chessboard with the property that any two distinct squares in the subset contain rooks in harmonious positions.
figure_description: Parity condition for pairs of rook positions on a chessboard.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let
$$p(x)=x^2-2.$$
For a positive integer $n$, define the sequence
$$a_0,a_1,a_2,\ldots$$
by setting
$$a_0=n$$
and
$$a_{k+1}=p(a_k)$$
for all $k\ge0$. Determine, with proof, all values of $n$ for which there exists $k\ge0$ such that
$$a_k=0.$$

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Construct triangle $ABC$ from a point $P$ in its interior as follows: draw rays $AP,BP,$ and $CP$. Let $W$ and $Z$ be the points where rays $BP$ and $CP$ intersect line $AC$, respectively. Likewise, let $X$ and $U$ be the points where rays $CP$ and $AP$ intersect line $BA$, respectively, and let $Y$ and $V$ be the points where rays $AP$ and $BP$ intersect line $CB$, respectively. Prove that one can choose points $A,B,$ and $C$ so that the quadrilaterals $PXCY,PZAU,$ and $WVBP$ are cyclic if and only if
$$
\frac{PW}{BV}= rac{PZ}{CU}= rac{PX}{AW}.
$$
figure_description: Interior-point construction with six intersection points and cyclic quadrilaterals.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A game is played on a regular $13$-gon whose vertices are initially colored blue. In each move, one may choose three vertices forming an isosceles triangle with all sides of nonzero length and flip the color of all three vertices. Determine whether there exists a sequence of moves after which all vertices are red.
figure_description: Color-flipping game on the vertices of a regular 13-gon.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let
$$x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$$
be a sequence of nonnegative integers such that
$$x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n=n$$
and
$$x_1+2x_2+\cdots+nx_n=n.$$
Prove that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{x_i}{i+1}
\le
\frac n2.
$$
